question: Does the 3 include frequency in grammars? DCS as well 4th?

answer.three_are: Aṣṭādhyāyī-internal structural positions (pc / an / ad), not three corpora
answer.dcs_in_original: indirect only (function-word exclusion principle from DIFFICULTY_ORDERING_RESULT.md); never a measured column
recommended_taxonomy: Axis A - structural demand: pc, an, ad (3 channels, one text)
Axis B - grammatical discourse: vyākaraṇa corpus df/tf (channel G) + DSG lexicographic salience (channel L)
Axis C - general literary register: DCS (channel D), a control, not a ranking signal

dcs.note: DCS-2026 lemma RANKING table; the fuller DCS export is 5,688,416 tokens / 90,349 lemmas per SanskritLexicography/RussianTranslation/release/fixture/dcs_freq.ttl. Counts here are the locally pinned ranking list.

G_grammar_corpus.unit: one Sanskrit passage / chunk / verse / sūtra-gloss

L_dsg_salience.matching_rule: Document frequency over the 4,383 DSG entries. For folded stems of <=4 characters an exact token match (?<![a-z])stem(?![a-z]) is used; longer stems use substring matching so that inflected forms count. Applied identically to the folded English and Russian definitions. Devanagari headwords are matched by substring against dev_variants() (class-nasal <-> anusvara). English prose is an UPPER BOUND for short Latin stems because English 'it', 'ca', 'na' collide; the Russian-prose and headword counts are reported alongside as collision controls.

hk_vs_slp1.issue: DSG column labelled `slp1` is Harvard-Kyoto, not SLP1
hk_vs_slp1.fix: raw value kept in `hk`; SLP1 derived from HK or IAST; class-nasal <-> anusvara variants generated for DCS joins

data_quality.rule: DSG `HK` is never joined to DCS directly. A single-pass longest-match HK->SLP1 conversion (or IAST->SLP1 when HK is blank/dirty) produces the canonical key; slp1_variants() adds class-nasal <-> anusvara spellings; the best-attested spelling is used (variants are alternative spellings, not independent lemmas, so counts are not summed).
